data.why: No pretrained model or raw spreadsheet ships with the repo, so a small synthetic SMILES+ratio+K training set was written to the repo root (seed/training_data.csv -> /work/app/training_data.csv) to drive scripts/train_model.py during install and produce the artifacts the Streamlit app reads; separate upload-ready CSVs exercise calibration and batch prediction, including an invalid-SMILES and a zero-sum-ratio row.

goals: Predict the column-chromatography K-value for a new compound (SMILES) at a chosen four-solvent (hexane:ethyl acetate:methanol:water) mixing ratio
Calibrate the zero-shot prediction for a specific compound against 1-5 of the scientist's own measured K-values and see the before/after error change

Batch-predict K for a list of compounds and ratios from an uploaded spreadsheet, including flagging invalid SMILES or malformed ratios, and compute pairwise separation factors (alpha) within compound pairs
Get a recommended solvent ratio that would hit a target K for a compound, optionally excluding ratios already tried or that failed
Inspect model comparison, residual and feature-importance/partial-dependence plots to judge whether the underlying model is trustworthy before relying on its predictions

review.summary: This tree matches the README's purpose and the app's five tabs well: predict K from SMILES and a solvent ratio, batch-predict with separation factors, calibrate with 1–5 measured points, recommend ratios for a target K, and check the model first. Every screen I sampled supports its node. It needs small fixes before filing: regroup the single-point calibration task, add the missing data-overview feature, and correct two feature descriptions.
